source.title: New results and open questions for SIR-PH epidemic models with linear birth rate, loss of immunity, vaccination, and disease and vaccination fatalities

accepted.question_text: Consider deterministic epidemic models with standard incidence and linear birth rate b(N)=Lambda N, one susceptible compartment S, one removed or immunized compartment R, and an n-dimensional vector I of disease compartments. In the SIR-PH class, disease-state transitions are encoded by a matrix A, infection forces by a matrix B, disease-induced mortality by a vector delta, loss of immunity by gamma_r, and vaccination by gamma_s. The first approximation SIR-PH-FA drops the quadratic fatality terms in the scaled equations, while the intermediate approximation SIR-PH-IA keeps the fatality terms in the susceptible and removed equations but not in the infectious equations. For the scaled SIR-PH, SIR-PH-FA, and SIR-PH-IA classes, does the condition R0>1 always imply that there is exactly one biologically feasible endemic equilibrium with positive disease components?
accepted.context_brief: Endemic-equilibrium existence and uniqueness for SIR-PH variants

evidence.quote: Our paper presents three new classes of models: SIR-PH, SIR-PH-FA, and SIR-PH-IA, and states two problems we would like to solve about them.

However, it is quite common that
1. When R0 > 1, there exists a unique fixed endemic point, and
2. the endemic point is locally stable when R0 > 1.

The model (3.5) with Φs = Φi = Φr = 1 will be called scaled model (SM ).
2. The model (3.5) with Φs = Φi = Φr = 0 will be called first approximation (FA ).
3. The model (3.5) with Φs = Φr = 1, Φi = 0 will be called intermediate approximation (IA ).

Remark 13 A yet another open problem is whether the endemic point must always exists for the FA and
IA models.

accepted.question_text: For SIR-PH epidemic models and their SIR-PH-FA and SIR-PH-IA approximations with linear births, vaccination, loss of immunity, and disease-induced mortality, does R0>1 always imply local asymptotic stability of the endemic equilibrium whenever such a biologically feasible endemic equilibrium exists?
accepted.context_brief: Local stability of endemic equilibria for SIR-PH variants

evidence.quote: However, the second property, the sufficiency of R0 > 1 for the local stability of an endemic point, remains open even for SIR-PH-FA models, despite the numerous particular cases in which it was checked to hold (via Routh-Hurwitz time-onerous computations, or Lyapunov functions).
Remark 8 We conjecture that the endemic point is always locally stable when 1 < R0.

However, the check of the sum of the second and third order principal leading minors of the Jacobian at
EE, and of the additional Hurwitz criterion, seemed to exceed our machine power.

accepted.question_text: For the varying-population SEIRS/SAIRS model with vaccination studied as the special case beta_e=0, e_r=0, gamma_r=0, gamma_s>=0, linear birth rate Lambda, and disease-induced death rate delta, let R0=s_dfe R where s_dfe=Lambda/(Lambda+gamma_s) and R is the corresponding reproduction factor without vaccination. In the regime R0<1<R, where the disease-free equilibrium is locally stable but R exceeds one, is the disease-free equilibrium globally asymptotically stable, and what Lyapunov function gives the most effective proof?
accepted.context_brief: Disease-free global stability when R0<1<R in the vaccinated varying-population SEIRS case

accepted.question_text: For the vaccinated varying-population SEIRS/SAIRS model in which existing theorems prove global stability of a unique endemic point only under certain parameter restrictions, can stable periodic solutions occur outside those proven global-stability cases?
accepted.context_brief: Possible stable periodic solutions outside known SEIRS global-stability regimes

evidence.quote:
[48, Thm 2.1] establishes global stability of a unique endemic point, in certain cases, and
suggest that outside those cases, "there may exist stable periodic solutions".

accepted.question_text: For a SEIRS epidemic model with disease fatalities in a growing population, no vaccination (gamma_s=0), and waning immunity gamma_r>=0, does R0>1 imply that the model has exactly one endemic equilibrium and that this endemic equilibrium is globally asymptotically stable?
accepted.context_brief: Endemic uniqueness and global stability with disease fatalities and waning immunity

evidence.quote:
Seven years later, [10] revisited the [34] problem with gamma_s = 0 and waning immunity gamma_r >= 0
(denoted by rho). The authors remark that in this particular case, there are still open questions:
"We have not proved, but we strongly believe that if R0 > 1, then the system (2.2) has one and
only one endemic equilibrium, and that this equilibrium is globally asymptotically stable."

accepted.question_text: For the eight-parameter constant-population SAIRS model obtained by setting the disease-induced death rate delta to zero, with vaccination, loss of immunity, exposed/asymptomatic transmission beta_e, and infective transmission beta_i, can global stability of the unique endemic equilibrium be proved beyond the currently resolved case beta_e<gamma?
accepted.context_brief: Global stability for the constant-population SAIRS model beyond beta_e<gamma

accepted.question_text: For the scaled SEIRS model with beta_e=0, e_r=0, vaccination rate gamma_s>=0, loss-of-immunity rate gamma_r>=0, linear birth rate Lambda, and disease-induced death rate delta, does R0>1 imply uniqueness of the endemic point and local stability of that endemic point, even in the special case beta_e=e_r=gamma_s=0?
accepted.context_brief: SEIRS scaled-model uniqueness and local stability after correction of a prior proof

evidence.quote:
The uniqueness of the endemic point and its local stability when R0 > 1 was also claimed in [37], and we
conjecture that these results are true, even for SEIRS, with beta_e = e_r = 0, gamma_s >= 0, gamma_r >= 0.

However, this must be viewed as an open problem even in the case beta_e = e_r = 0 = gamma_s, since the crucial
analog of (5.3), the equation [37, (3.28)] used intensively in their proof is wrong.

accepted.question_text: For SIR-PH models with linear birth rate, loss of immunity, vaccination, and disease-induced mortality, can the determinant identity Det(J_ee)=-Det(J_dfe), established for lower-dimensional SAIR first-approximation cases, be extended by exploiting the block partition of the scaled-model Jacobian into the susceptible coordinate and disease-coordinate block?
accepted.context_brief: Extension of the endemic/disease-free determinant formula to SIR-PH models

accepted.question_text: How can the endemic-equilibrium and stability theory for SIR-PH-type epidemic models be extended to models with two or more susceptible compartments that can become infected, such as SEIT-type models?
accepted.context_brief: Multiple susceptible compartments in SIR-PH-type epidemic models

evidence.quote:
Study the case of two or more compartments susceptible to become infected (for example the SEIT
model [51, 39]).

accepted.question_text: Can the scaled epidemic model with linear births and disease-induced fatalities be rigorously analyzed as a perturbation of the first approximation model, for example using slow-fast, singular-perturbation, or homogenization techniques, so that conclusions about endemic equilibria and stability can transfer from the approximation to the scaled model?
accepted.context_brief: Scaled model as perturbation of the first approximation

evidence.quote:
The well-studied classic
models may then be recovered via a heuristic "first approximation" (FA) of ignoring the extra
terms. This approximation, which deserves being investigated rigorously via slow-fast/singular
perturbation/homogeneization techniques, has the merit of putting under one umbrella constant
and varying population models with linear birth rates.
Study the scaled model as a perturbation of the FA model.

accepted.question_text: Can the geometric approach to stability associated with Li, Graef, Wang, Karsai, Muldowney, and Lu be used to prove endemic-equilibrium stability for SIR-PH, SIR-PH-FA, SIR-PH-IA, or SAIRS models in parameter regimes where Routh-Hurwitz and Lyapunov computations are currently difficult?
accepted.context_brief: Geometric stability methods for SIR-PH and SAIRS models

evidence.quote:
As the authors explain, the difficulties met, especially in the global stability problem,
forced them to devise new ingenious methods.
Study stability via the geometric approach of Li, Graef, Wang, Karsai, Muldoney and Lu [31].

accepted.question_text: Can global asymptotic stability be proved for the ten-parameter SAIR/V+S model with standard incidence, linear birth rate, susceptible S, exposed/asymptomatic E, infective I, recovered/vaccinated R, vaccination, loss of immunity, exposed and infective transmission, and disease-induced deaths, rather than being supported only by numerical simulations?
accepted.context_brief: Global stability for the full ten-parameter SAIR/V+S model

evidence.quote:
We generalize the uniqueness of the endemic point and the local stability results of these six papers,
and at the same time draw attention to certain unnecessary assumptions and mistakes. The hardest
issue, that of global stability, is only illustrated via some numerical simulations.

In this paper, we consider a ten parameters SAIR (also called SEIR in the classic literature [51])
epidemic model inspired by [24, 31, 34, 48, 10, 37, 16, 40], which we call SAIR/V+S (or SAIR
for short), since it groups together immunized people in an R/V compartment.
